phrases.latin: Avia linteum candidum strāvit; Theodōrus mappās quattuor et patellās quattuor et cochleāria disposuit; pater, argenteīs ēscāriīs ē māchinā ēlūtōriā prōmptīs, furcillās, cultrōs, pōcula, urceum aquae, salīnum, piperīnum; duae candēlae accēnsae sunt
phrases.english: Grandma spread a white tablecloth; Theo set out four napkins, four plates and the spoons; Dad took the silver cutlery out of the dishwasher and set out the forks, knives, glasses, a jug of water, the salt and the pepper; two candles were lit

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 125, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
